claim: For the stationary symmetric two-state HMM with unknown lambda,m in [1/2,3/4], two lag-product statistics from one length-T raw path yield E[(lambdahat-lambda)^2+(mhat-m)^2] bounded by 65863/(4T), and the fitted predictor has expected worst-finite-history one-step TV <385/sqrt(T), one-step KL <=1354896/T, and H-step conditional future KL <=1354896 H/T.
interface: One stationary raw observation stream Y_1,...,Y_T; no hidden labels, resets, selected-word queries, interventions, or parameter values. The known class is the symmetric two-state HMM with lambda,m in [1/2,3/4].
cost: T symbols, one initial stationary start, O(T) time, O(log T) counter bits plus two parameters, O(|h|) prediction time; precision and fixed-point rounding budgets in RESULT.txt section 8.
baseline: A full-path estimator can compute the same moments and reproduce the learner; the lower bound FPUT-2 applies to every raw-path estimator.
limitations: Structured two-state class with fixed positive margins and known family; not a theorem for arbitrary HMMs, unknown rank, or vanishing singular gaps. Novelty and external proof validation are UNKNOWN.

claim: For T>=15, every estimator of the full raw path has worst-finite-history one-step TV risk at least (25/1024)*sqrt(7/(32(T-1))) and one-step KL risk at least 4375/(16777216(T-1)); these lower bounds also apply to any H-step conditional future KL loss for H>=1.
interface: Same class and raw-stream interface as FPUT-1. The comparison uses a local transition-parameter pair with a common emission parameter.
proof: RESULT.txt section 9; full hidden-path KL, data processing, Pinsker, and Le Cam reduction are given.
cost: The raw data are the complete T-symbol path; the KL upper bound also holds if hidden states are revealed, so no learner with less information can evade it.
baseline: Information-theoretic lower bound for any full-data method, including full likelihood and arbitrary postprocessing.
limitations: The lower bound is a fixed-margin parametric local alternative; it does not characterize arbitrary-HMM or growing-horizon KL minimax dependence.

claim: For this symmetric two-state HMM only, each lag-k product Y_t Y_(t+k) is a function of k iid hidden transition increments and two iid emission signs; products at start-time separation d>k are independent. Therefore its sample mean variance is at most (1+2k)/(T-k).
interface: Stationary hidden chain with symmetric transition correlation lambda and conditionally independent emissions as in FPUT-1.
proof: RESULT.txt section 5 proves Y_t=S_t E_t and Y_tY_(t+k)=E_t E_(t+k) product D_j, including cancellation of the initial hidden sign.
cost: No asymptotic mixing approximation; exact finite dependence for the specified lag-product sequence.
baseline: Generic finite-state HMM observation processes need not be finite-dependent; this proof is not transferred by geometric mixing alone.
limitations: Special symmetry and binary-state factorization are essential; generic-HMM covariance control remains UNKNOWN.
